title: Jensen Huang allies build a "war room" to get him back at Nvidia
gist: Days after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO over affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate, allies including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker are campaigning for his reinstatement, while Treasury's Scott Bessent demands a leadership shake-up and interim CEO Colette Kress steadies the $4 trillion company before earnings.

insights.claim: Jensen Huang is discussing a possible comeback as Nvidia CEO, and an ally is assembling a Silicon Valley executive 'war room' to lobby the board and seek White House support.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A Huang return would be a major sentiment catalyst for NVDA; track board and White House signals.
insights.locator: One Huang ally told the FT

insights.claim: Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney are among executives backing a public letter demanding Nvidia's board 'Bring Jensen Back', and some Nvidia employees have publicly signed on.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Broad industry and employee backing raises the odds of Huang's reinstatement and signals talent-retention risk if he stays out.
insights.locator: A public campaign to reinstate Huang

insights.claim: Nvidia shareholders Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management urged the board to keep all options open including Huang's return, citing his long track record and massive uncertainty from his departure.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Large institutional holders are pushing for continuity, a positioning signal on how the buy side views the leadership vacuum.
insights.quote: all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang

insights.claim: A Huang ally claimed that everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen, implying the AI labs are a notable exception.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Hints at friction between Nvidia and frontier AI labs, its biggest customers.
insights.quote: Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen

insights.claim: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a 'dramatic shake-up' in Nvidia leadership, signaling Washington pushback against Huang's reinstatement.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Political opposition makes a Huang return less likely and raises regulatory risk for Nvidia.

insights.claim: Unlike other founder-CEOs, Huang lacked a controlling shareholding and could not overrule Nvidia's board, which with interim CEO Colette Kress aims to steady the company ahead of Tuesday's quarterly results.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Board control, not founder control, decides the outcome; earnings call is the near-term volatility event.
insights.locator: Huang, who lacked the controlling shareholding

insights.claim: Even allies of Jensen Huang concede that his affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense, complicating his rehabilitation.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Governance grounds for the exit are hard to dismiss, weighing on reinstatement odds.
insights.quote: Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense

insights.claim: Nvidia's board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Huang, though the board said no formal process had begun.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A Haas appointment would affect both Nvidia and Arm leadership; watch for succession announcements.

insights.claim: Huang's affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, has intensified scrutiny of Nvidia's compliance when selling AI chips to Asian customers with potential China links.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Expect tighter export compliance and potential sales friction for Nvidia in Asia.

insights.claim: The leadership crisis at the $4 trillion chip company Nvidia is under an independent board probe into the conduct that led to Huang's resignation.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Probe findings are a binary catalyst for Nvidia's governance and leadership outlook.
